Maintenance Report — MNT-0139-005

Asset: WELL-0139 (NE-07 Well 139, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 10 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 Jun 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 62 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0139-0034 on 2023-06-08 Report written: 13 Jun 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0139-0034 showed the wellhead at 33.6 °C with the air at 32.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 348 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 278 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0139-005 (WS-06).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0139-007

Asset: WELL-0139 (NE-07 Well 139, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 05 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Aug 2023 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 409 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0139-0042 on 2023-08-03 Report written: 22 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0139-0042 showed the wellhead at 39.5 °C with the air at 37.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0139-021

Asset: WELL-0139 (NE-07 Well 139, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 30 Aug 2025 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0139-0144 on 2025-08-28 Report written: 31 Aug 2025

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0139-0144 at 11:15 on 2025-08-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.5% of the pad area, estimated 4.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 348 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 278 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0139-021 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.55% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Asset: WELL-0139 (NE-07 Well 139, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 30 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 31 Jan 2026 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 21 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0139-0163 on 2026-01-29 Report written: 31 Jan 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0139-0163 at 08:15 on 2026-01-29 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.0% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 348 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 278 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.
